root_cause: N+1 query explosion introduced by v5.2.0 serializer rewrite
root_cause_detail: v5.2.0 removed the ProductVariant prefetch and lazy-loads variants per item. A 50-item category page became ~1180 database queries, pinning application CPU at 97% (throttling 31% of requests) and driving postgres-catalog CPU to 96%. Nothing is saturated except CPU; the pool waits are a symptom, not the cause.
resolution: Rolled catalog-api back to v5.1.4, restoring the prefetch. CPU 31%, DB queries/min 940, category p95 230ms. The serializer rewrite is being re-landed behind a query-count assertion.
contributing_factors: No query-count assertion in the serializer test suite, so an N+1 shape shipped to production
Canary was 2% for 90 seconds - not enough time to accumulate per-item queries
CPU throttling masked the error rate, so the page looked 'only degraded' rather than broken
Database CPU was blamed before the application's own CPU was checked
prevention: Fail CI when queries-per-request for a route grows more than 2x
Require a 15-minute canary soak for serializer and ORM changes
Alert on CPU throttling percentage, not only on CPU utilisation
Add a per-request query budget to the service template
runbook_changes: Add step 1: compare queries-per-request against baseline before anything else
Add 'CPU + query volume together usually means a code-path change, not a dependency' to the runbook
Remove the generic 'scale out to relieve CPU' advice - it moves the load to the database
lessons: Restarts do not fix a CPU problem caused by code: CPU returned to 97% within 30 seconds of the restart.
Scaling out during a CPU saturation incident pushes the same query storm into the database, which was already at 96% CPU.
queries-per-request is the single highest-information metric for a CPU saturation incident.
A low error rate does not mean the service is fine - catalog-api throttled 31% of requests instead of failing them.
first_checks: which release changed the request path and when
is the database CPU high because of us (query volume) or on its own
confirmed_by: CPU below 60% and queries-per-request below 50 for 5 minutes
memory_episode: INC-D1 (catalog-api, SEV-2): CPU 97% with 31% throttling, category pages 8.9s, 1180 queries per request eleven minutes after v5.2.0 removed the ProductVariant prefetch (N+1). Postgres CPU 96% was a side effect. Resolved by rolling back to v5.1.4. Check first next time: queries-per-request against baseline, then the deploy diff.
memory_service_pattern: catalog-api's characteristic failure is a CPU saturation incident with an N+1 query shape after a serializer/ORM change. Symptoms: high service CPU, throttling instead of errors, database CPU high as a side effect, and healthy caches. Restarting and scaling out are both wrong.
